details:
**Tom Robinson's trial for the rape of Mayella Ewell**
The novel centers on this trial. Tom Robinson, a Black man, is falsely accused of raping Mayella Ewell, a poor white woman. Her father Bob Ewell backs the accusation, and an all-white jury convicts Tom even though the evidence shows he is innocent. After the trial Bob Ewell spits in Atticus's face, and Tom is later shot 17 times while trying to escape from prison.

**Atticus Finch, lawyer in Maycomb, Alabama**
Atticus is the widowed lawyer who defends Tom Robinson. He is the father of the narrator, Jean Louise "Scout" Finch, and her older brother Jem. The book is set in the 1930s in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama. An earlier draft of the novel was published in 2015 as *Go Set a Watchman*.

**Boo Radley**
Arthur "Boo" Radley is the Finches' reclusive neighbor. Town rumor says he once stabbed his father with a pair of scissors. Scout, Jem and their summer friend Dill are obsessed with him and try to lure him out, for example by trying to leave a note on his windowsill with a fishing pole. At the end he turns out to be the children's quiet protector.

**Scout's ham costume and Bob Ewell's attack after the Halloween pageant**
At a school Halloween pageant about Maycomb County, Scout plays a ham. She misses her cue to come on stage, and on the walk home the costume keeps her from running when Bob Ewell attacks her and Jem in revenge for the trial. Jem's arm is broken, which explains the crooked arm mentioned in the novel's first line. Boo Radley kills Ewell and carries Jem home. Earlier that night, classmate Cecil Jacobs jumps out and scares the children on their way to the pageant.

**Mrs. Dubose and her camellias**
Mrs. Dubose is a cranky, racist old woman who lives near the Finches. After she insults Atticus, Jem cuts the tops off her camellia bushes. As punishment he has to read to her every afternoon until she dies. Atticus later explains that she was fighting her morphine addiction, and he calls her the bravest person he knew.

**"One-Shot Finch" and the rabid dog Tim Johnson**
A neighbor's dog, Tim Johnson, goes mad with rabies and wanders down the street. The maid Calpurnia warns the neighbors. Sheriff Heck Tate hands his rifle to Atticus, who kills the dog with one shot. Miss Maudie then tells the surprised children that their father was once known as "One-Shot Finch," the best shot in the county.

**The lynch mob at the jail and Mr. Cunningham**
The night before the trial, Atticus guards Tom at the Maycomb jail, and a mob led by Mr. Cunningham comes for Tom. Scout, Jem and Dill have sneaked out to watch. Scout innocently chats with Mr. Cunningham about his entailment, his son Walter, and how he paid Atticus for legal work with hickory nuts and firewood. Embarrassed, he breaks up the mob.

**Tom Robinson's useless left arm and the chiffarobe**
Tom's left arm was crippled in a cotton gin accident when he was a boy. Mayella's bruises are on the right side of her face, which means a left-handed person hit her, and Atticus shows that Bob Ewell is left-handed. Tom says Mayella asked him to bust up an old chiffarobe (a wardrobe-dresser) and then tried to kiss him. The prosecutor mocks him by asking if he is good at "busting up chiffarobes" with one hand.

**Gifts in the tree knothole**
Scout and Jem find small gifts in the knothole of an oak tree by the Radley house. They include chewing gum, Indian-head pennies, twine, soap carvings of the two children, a spelling medal and a pocket watch. The children realize the gifts come from Boo, but his brother Nathan fills the hole with cement.

**Dolphus Raymond's Coca-Cola in a paper sack**
Dolphus Raymond is a wealthy white man who lives with a Black woman and has mixed-race children. He drinks Coca-Cola out of a paper sack so the town thinks he is a drunk, which gives people an excuse for how he lives. During the trial he gives the upset Dill a sip.

**Walter Cunningham and the molasses**
On Scout's first day of school, she tries to explain the poor Cunningham family to her new teacher, Miss Caroline Fisher, and gets her hand slapped with a ruler. Later, when Walter Cunningham comes home with the Finches for dinner, he pours molasses all over his food. Scout makes a rude comment, and Calpurnia scolds her for being bad-mannered to a guest.

**Miss Maudie's house fire and the blanket**
One winter night, the house of the Finches' neighbor Miss Maudie Atkinson burns down. While Scout stands outside watching, someone puts a blanket around her shoulders without her noticing. The family later realizes it was Boo Radley.

**Heck Tate's cover-up and "a sin to kill a mockingbird"**
After Bob Ewell's body is found with a knife in his ribs, Sheriff Heck Tate insists that Ewell "fell on his knife" so that the shy Boo will not be put in the public eye. Scout agrees, saying that exposing Boo would be like shooting a mockingbird. This connects to the title: Atticus calls killing mockingbirds a sin, and Miss Maudie explains that they "don't do one thing but sing their hearts out."

**Calpurnia and First Purchase church**
Calpurnia, the Finches' Black cook, takes Scout and Jem to her church, First Purchase African M.E. Church. It got its name because freed slaves paid for it with their first earnings. Since few members can read, Calpurnia's son Zeebo, the town garbage collector, leads the hymns by reading out each line first.

**The "colored" balcony and Reverend Sykes**
At the crowded trial, Reverend Sykes of First Purchase saves seats for Scout, Jem and Dill in the courthouse's segregated "colored" balcony. They watch Atticus's defense of Tom from there. Calpurnia later finds them there, which upsets her.
